source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 20: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer:
Do not select tensor or pipeline parallelism from a generic rule. State the target latency SLA, including p99, throughput and concurrency, model checkpoint and sequence-length mix, GPU count/type and memory budget, interconnect topology, runtime versions, availability objective, and whether reconfiguration is permitted. Treat the checkpoint, tokenizer, decoding, request trace, placement, power limits, scheduler, batching policy, and load generator as assumptions to verify; freeze them and vary only the parallelism strategy plus preregistered feasible layer partitions and microbatch settings.

Make the hypothesis numerical and falsifiable for the scenario variant 20: at a declared offered load, one strategy will reduce p99 end-to-end latency by a stated margin while remaining within quality, error-rate, memory, and availability gates. Run randomized interleaved paired trials with identical requests, equal warm-up and compilation, fixed sample size, documented exclusions and stopping rules, and disjoint tuning versus held-out workloads. Measure per-GPU memory/utilization, tensor communication bytes/time, synchronization waits, pipeline bubbles, queueing, TTFT and TPOT in milliseconds, end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput in requests/s and tokens/s, energy/cost, timeouts, OOMs, stragglers, failed-rank recovery, and reconfiguration time. Report raw metrics, units, confidence intervals, and stratified results by sequence length, batch, concurrency, topology, and injected fault.

Control confounders such as cache state, thermal throttling, compiler effects, placement, background load, request ordering, and retry behavior. Do not expose production data without authorization; use redacted or synthetic traces and isolate trials. Reject a rollout if quality, safety, error, memory, or availability gates fail, or if the latency margin is not supported on held-out data. Canary the chosen configuration, monitor regressions and fault recovery, and keep a versioned configuration plus an immediate rollback to the last known-good strategy. These are experimental assumptions and evidence requirements, not measured platform facts.
